source_anchors.locator: Surah 108:2, vol. 20, printed p. 195, online lines 955-958
source_anchors.supports: Qurtubi explicitly introduces the material with قال ابن العربي and encloses the Malik passage as a quotation; this witness reads صلاة يوم النحر without الصبح.

source_anchors.locator: Surah al-Kawthar:2, vol. 4, printed pp. 395-396, online lines 1056-1071
source_anchors.supports: The text places فأما مالك فقال before the no-heard-report statement and inference; it resumes Ibn al-Arabi's authorial commentary with قال القاضي رضي الله عنه, explains والذي أراد مالك, and later marks his separate preference with والذي عندي. This is literary nested attribution, not an oral isnad.

findings.voice_chain: Al-Qurtubi reports Ibn al-Arabi's passage; within that passage Malik is the quoted speaker for ما سمعت فيه شيئا and the inference introduced by والذي يقع في نفسي. Ibn al-Arabi then explains Malik's reasoning and separately states his own preference.
findings.negative_provenance: ما سمعت فيه شيئا remains Malik's reported statement that he had heard no transmitted explanation concerning the verse; it must not be presented as a received Prophetic tafsir.
findings.route_boundary: Neither Qurtubi's quotation nor Ibn al-Arabi's cited passage supplies a full transmission chain for Malik's statement. No oral route is reconstructed.
findings.wording_difference: The Qurtubi witness/live row has صلاة يوم النحر; Ibn al-Arabi's own displayed work has صلاة الصبح يوم النحر. This is a cross-work textual difference in these digital presentations; cause, edition relationship, and manuscript status remain unestablished.
findings.translation_boundary: The existing English follows the shorter stored Qurtubi wording. Do not add 'dawn' from Ibn al-Arabi's own work to the Qurtubi translation without edition-specific human review.
findings.authorship_boundary: Ibn al-Arabi's own preference marked by والذي عندي belongs to Ibn al-Arabi, not Malik or al-Qurtubi; no personal adoption by Qurtubi is inferred.
findings.independent_source_limit: These electronic text presentations provide source-specific locators but do not establish manuscript ancestry, historical authenticity, or live source_url 671's edition mapping.
